title: The Thermostat Rule
trend: First cold snap of November (Instagram Reels 'November' cold-weather clips Rising 142K, SocialPilot Instagram Reels trends Nov 17-25 2026, US) + the yearly 'no heat until December' household rule — absurd-rule skit: Dad Frank in shorts enforces 'no heat until December first' while teen Lena wears three hoodies, Mom reads in oven mitts and the dog sleeps in the dryer; twist: the hallway thermostat is a fake (tape and a sticky note, 'Do not tell Lena') he put up in twenty fifteen to end arguments, and the real one heats the garage to seventy six where he sits in a recliner with pudding — Mom has the other recliner; button: everyone moves to the garage, Lena gets a beanbag, and the fake thermostat finally gets a job
youtube_title: My dad says no heat until December. Then I found out where he goes every night 🥶
description:
It is thirty one degrees and Dad says the heat stays off until December first. Lena is in three hoodies and the dog sleeps in the dryer. Then the thermostat starts talking.

#cartoon #animation #funny #winter #shorts
tiktok_caption: house rule: no heat until december. it is thirty one degrees 🥶 #cartoon #animation #funny #winter

lines.text: Dad. It is thirty one degrees outside. I can see my breath. Indoors.
House rule number one. The heat does not go on until December first.
Hello. I am the thermostat. Nobody has touched me since March.
I am wearing three hoodies. The third one is yours.
Then you are warm. And I am cold. That is called parenting.
Why are you wearing shorts?
Because I am built different. I am a furnace with feet.
His knees are blue. I can see them from the wall.
Mom is wearing oven mitts to read a book.
Your mother loves mitts.
The dog is sleeping inside the dryer.
He is a smart dog. He found the warm spot.
That is the problem. There is only one warm spot. And it is the dryer.
House rule number two. If you are cold, do jumping jacks.
I did forty. Now I am sweaty and cold. Like a soup that gave up.
Can I just say, I would love to work. I have been on vacation since spring.
Okay. I am turning it up. Two degrees. Just two.
Step away from the thermostat.
I am pressing the button.
Ooh. That tickles. Again.
It says seventy. I hear nothing. No whoosh. No heat.
Huh. Must be broken. Guess we wait until December.
Dad. Why are you smiling?
I always smile. I am a happy, cold man.
Lena. I have to tell you something. I am not connected to anything.
What?
There are no wires behind me. Just tape. And one sticky note.
What does the sticky note say?
Do not tell Lena.
Dad!
Okay. Okay. In twenty fifteen, your mother and I fought over that thing every day.
She wanted seventy four. I wanted sixty two. So I bought a fake one.
You put up a fake thermostat?
For peace. Everybody presses it. Everybody feels heard. Nobody wins.
Then where is the real one?
In the garage.
The garage. Where you go every night to fix the lawn mower.
It is a very complicated lawn mower.
There is no lawn mower. There is a recliner. And a blanket with sleeves.
You have a heated garage?
Seventy six degrees. And a little fridge with pudding.
We are freezing in here, and you are out there in a recliner eating pudding?
I wear shorts in here so you think I am tough.
Then I go out there and I am a different man.
His knees turn pink again. It is beautiful. It is like spring.
I am telling Mom.
Your mother knows.
She knows?
She has the other recliner. The oven mitts are a cover story.
So the only people freezing in this house are me and the dog.
The dog found out last week. That is why he lives in the dryer. He is protesting.
Okay. New house rule. Everybody goes to the garage.
Do I get a recliner?
You get a beanbag. You earn the recliner.
And the pudding?
Pudding is for people who kept the secret.
So I have to stay in here? Alone? Being pressed?
Don't worry. Somebody will press you tomorrow.
Finally. A job.
